request.spec: Return 'initials' as the upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot, e.g. 'J.S.'.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Return 'initials' as the upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot, e.g. 'J.S.'.

agent.result_text:
Done. The full build is green.

## Summary

I implemented the `initials` field — the upper-cased first letters of `firstName` and `lastName`, dot-separated with a trailing dot (e.g. `J.S.`).

Two changes:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `initials` string property to the `Owner` schema (which generates `OwnerDto`), alongside the existing `displayName`.

2. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — added a MapStruct `@Mapping` that computes `initials` from the owner's first and last name:
   ```java
   @Mapping(target = "initials", expression = "java(Character.toUpperCase(owner.getFirstName().charAt(0)) + \".\" + Character.toUpperCase(owner.getLastName().charAt(0)) + \".\")")
   ```

The field flows out through the existing `RespondWithOwner` function → `OwnerMapper.toOwnerDto` → the GET `/api/owners/{id}` response, so no endpoint wiring changes were needed. `AcceptanceTest.coreComputesInitials` (asserting `$.initials` == `"J.S."` for "john"/"smith") passes, and the full suite reports `BUILD SUCCESS`.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The new `initials` mapping follows the exact idiom already established one line above it: the `displayName` derived field is likewise computed via an inline `@Mapping(... expression = "java(...)")` on `toOwnerDto`. Placing another derived-display field in the same unit is coherent and additive — derived view fields live in the mapper, entities stay clean, and the OpenAI schema addition mirrors the adjacent `displayName` property block (title/description/type/readOnly/example). No duplication, and `OwnerMapper` isn't becoming a catch-all — this is precisely the kind of per-field derivation the interface exists for. A maintainer would find the two mappings sitting together natural.

(One readability note, not a structural defect and not blocking: the initials expression is denser than `displayName`. If the project later accumulates more or more complex derived fields, extracting a small default helper method on the mapper interface would be the idiomatic next step — but with only these two fields, matching the existing inline-expression pattern is the right call.)
